market_holds: Spot 42.96 at the 18:09 UTC seal; Yahoo's daily bar closes 2026-11-19 at 42.19, on a 40.26-44.85 range. Run-up is +5.5% over 5 days and -6.0% over 20; the stock is 23% below its 52-week high of 59.50 (the Berkshire spike on Oct 14) and well above the $29 IPO price. The front December straddle gives an event-implied move of 23.9%, but the ATM IV is 115% and the ATM spread is 31% of mid, so that figure is inflated. The one prior print (Q2, 2026-08-13) moved -4.4% at the open and -16.5% by the close. The options lean bearish: 25-delta put skew of +14 vol points and put/call open interest of 4.3. Short interest is 20.1m shares (3-6% of float, 2026-09-30 settlement). Q3 revenue consensus is about $740-746m (Earnings Whispers $740.3m, 2026-11-15), against a company guide of $733-745m that covers only businesses owned on 2026-08-12, so Airtable (closed 09-04) and Miro (closed 10-26) are excluded. Q3 EPS consensus is $0.26-0.32, and sources disagree on whether that is GAAP. The FY26 guide is $2.78-2.82B against a Street average of about $2.9B (range 2.8-3.1B). FY27 revenue at $4.26B shows that at least some models already carry Airtable and Miro. BofA (Underperform, PT $38, note of 2026-11-16) says buy-side expectations for Q3 revenue and adjusted operating income have fallen 'significantly' below the guide because of AI-disruption fears.
view: This print is mostly a mechanical reset rather than a test of hidden operating data. Reported Q3 will include about 27 days of Airtable (about $476m ARR, so roughly $35m), which the guide and most of the Q3 consensus exclude. The new FY outlook will add about four months of Airtable and two of Miro (about $600m ARR), which puts my arithmetic for the FY revenue guide near $3.0B against a Street average of $2.9B. The headline will therefore very likely read as a revenue beat and a guide raise. But every investor who follows the name knows the two deals closed, and the stock trades on organic growth and margins. Q2 organic growth was only +3%, with Remini and Splice declining (AI-exposed consumer apps), and the open questions are how much the acquired businesses dilute margins and how much leverage rises after $1.8B of 9.6%/8.6% secured notes. Q2 showed the same thing: a clean headline beat ($704m vs about $685m, EPS $0.46 vs $0.27) still produced -16.5%, because the FY guide sat below the Street and the stock had run up about 31% in the six sessions before on the Airtable deal. The setup this time differs in the direction that favours the stock. There is no run-up. The bar is depressed (BofA's buy-side read, the stock in the lower half of its range after the WSJ-driven sell-off in late September). Options pay for downside, so an in-line organic quarter with a mechanically higher guide could squeeze puts. Against that, the AI-exposure narrative, rising leverage, a December 28 lock-up (unconfirmed) and the Q2 pattern of fading through the session after the 08:00 call make the downside tail fat. I lean slightly up but cannot see the organic number before the company prints it, and nothing I found independently measures Q3 organic trends.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the mechanical boost: the Q3 consensus near the guide midpoint ($740m) appears to leave out Airtable's September stub, and BofA says buy-side expectations sit below even that. A headline beat plus a raised FY outlook is likely, but whether the price leaves it out is not shown, because sophisticated holders strip acquisitions out and the 13:00 ET window depends on how the organic and margin lines read on the call. No dated independent evidence of organic strength or weakness was found.

recommendation.reason: The likely headline beat and raise come from acquisitions the market knows closed. The line that decides the reaction, organic growth and margins after Airtable and Miro, has no independent trace I could read before the release. Depressed expectations and put-heavy positioning tilt the odds slightly up, but the Q2 precedent of a clean headline beat fading 16% inside the session keeps this well short of 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 organic growth below zero, or an FY adjusted operating income outlook that rises much less than revenue once Airtable and Miro are added (margin dilution), restated on the 08:00 ET call, would turn this down sharply.

self_critique: The strongest case against a mild up-lean: the Q2 precedent shows this stock sells off through the session after the 08:00 call even on clean beats. A new outlook that folds in Miro and Airtable invites scrutiny of organic decline and margin dilution, the AI-exposure narrative is fresh (BofA, WSJ), and leverage is rising at 9.6% coupons. The heavy put open interest may be holder hedging ahead of a December lock-up rather than a short to squeeze. Equally, the low bar may already be in the price at $42, below most targets but above BofA's $38.
approach_notes: The P6 instruction to find the line the last reaction traded on, plus reading the guide's exclusion language, framed this name well (a mechanical beat vs organic). P3's alternative-data list did not pay inside the time on a holding-company portfolio of many apps with no single-series proxy, and paywalled Italian press and the WSJ blocked the narrative check.
